chapter: Rhythm Club, studio dates and the 1930s big bands
title: Records cut in New York but released in Europe first
summary: Charlie Johnson's RCA sides were cut on 23rd Street; companies often issued jazz in Europe first because of the strong market.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe

the things that Charlie Johnson made back there years ago on RCA, they were cut down on 23rd Street -- those records.
But they were released in Europe. A lot of times they cut records here and they release them in Europe, because maybe their schedule is too busy here.
Or, they wanted some jazz for Europe so they would cut different jazz musicians, and they would release them in Europe first, and then release them back here.
A lot of times a lot of records were released -- when jazz records were released by these different companies in Europe.
But then they brought them back here and released them. Because you remember, the time we were having our Depression, the European market was big for jazz.
That's probably what you were talking about that happened with the Coleman Hawkins' Body and Soul.
